channel.title: SUBSUELO FS — Production guides
channel.description: Direct guides for music prompts, negative prompts and sound direction.

item.title: What is a negative prompt in music and when should you use one?
item.description: What it removes, where it goes and when it helps with vocals, instruments or finish.

item.title: How to write music prompts that give a clear direction
item.description: A practical structure for genre, pulse, drums, low end, source material, space and mix.

item.title: How to describe drums in a music prompt and avoid the default groove
item.description: Concrete vocabulary for describing drums in a music prompt: pocket, source families, swing, density and the mistakes that flatten a groove.

item.title: 808, sub-bass and movement: controlling the low end in a music prompt
item.description: Which words select a sub, an 808 or a bassline in a music prompt, how to describe movement, and how to clean a muddy low end with negative prompts.

item.title: Why AI music sounds generic and the prompt habits that fix it
item.description: Generic AI music comes from vague prompts averaged into the genre's middle. Source words, space, exclusions and one-axis iteration fix it.

item.title: Space, texture and dirt: writing the room into your prompt
item.description: Reverb space, echo, tape and degradation vocabulary for music prompts: dry vs washed, dub delay, vinyl crackle, and how much dirt is too much.
